channelId.description: channel-event: defaults to the current channel.

messageTemplate.description: channel-event (required): what the agent receives. Must not render empty.

inputMapping.description: start-flow: flow input → dot-path into the payload.

idempotencyKey.description: Same key twice → the first automation is returned, nothing duplicated.

tools.name: automate_schedule-reminder
tools.description: Remind at a given time: the message is delivered once to the channel (default: this conversation) and the agent acts on it. time: natural language ("tomorrow at 9am", "in 2 hours", "el lunes a las 10") or ISO 8601.

time.description: Natural language or ISO 8601, in the future.

message.description: What the agent receives when it fires (max 4000 chars).

channelId.description: Target channel (default: the current one).

timezone.description: IANA timezone the time is expressed in (default: env).

tools.name: automate_create-recurring-task
tools.description: Deliver a message to a channel on a recurring schedule (default channel: this conversation); the agent acts on it each time. schedule: natural language, PRIMARY ("cada lunes a las 9", "weekdays a las 8", "cada 2 horas"); cron: 5 fields "min hour day month weekday" (advanced).

schedule.description: Natural language (PRIMARY): "cada lunes a las 9", "weekdays a las 8", "cada 15 minutos", "el primer día de mes".

cron.description: Advanced: 5-field cron expression.

message.description: What the agent receives on each run (max 4000 chars).

channelId.description: Target channel (default: the current one).

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the cron (default: env).

name.description: Name in the Automate window (default: the message).

tools.name: automate_create-webhook
tools.description: Create a webhook: a secret URL external systems POST JSON to; each call runs the action (create a task — with discriminator dedupe —, message a channel, or start a flow). The URL is returned once.

name.description: Short name, e.g. "GitHub issues → tasks".

action.description: What happens. {type:"create-todo-item", parentId?, assignee?, state?, plannedDay?, plannedTime?, textTemplate, descriptionTemplate?, instructionsTemplate?} (creates a task in the to-do list / Tasks tree — parent group optional, assignee {kind:"agent"|"user", id}, plannedDay "YYYY-MM-DD") | {type:"create-task", projectId, agentId?, columnId?, titleTemplate, instructionsTemplate, descriptionTemplate?} (creates a task on a project board) | {type:"channel-event", channelId?, agentId?, messageTemplate} (defaults: current channel and agent) | {type:"start-flow", flowId, projectId, inputMapping?}. Templates: {{field}} / {{payload.field}} / {{topic}} / {{payload}} (JSON) / {{a || b || "literal"}} (first non-empty wins); nothing else ({{#if}} etc. is rejected). Required templates (title/instructions/message/text) must not render empty; the trigger payload becomes the task input artifact.

parentId.description: create-todo-item: parent group node ID (omit for root). Get IDs with the todo-list get-tree tool.

assignee.description: create-todo-item: { kind: "agent" | "user", id } — who does the task.

state.description: create-todo-item: initial state (default pending; blocked not allowed).

plannedDay.description: create-todo-item: "YYYY-MM-DD" — the day the task is planned for.

textTemplate.description: create-todo-item (required): task title, e.g. "Responder a {{payload.fromName}}". Must not render empty.

agentId.description: Defaults to the agent running the tool.

titleTemplate.description: create-task (required): task title, e.g. "Lead: {{fromName || fromId}}". Must not render empty.

instructionsTemplate.description: create-task (required): what the agent has to do. Must not render empty. The payload is also available to the agent as the task input artifact.

descriptionTemplate.description: create-task (optional): one-line human summary; empty render → no description.

channelId.description: channel-event: defaults to the current channel.

messageTemplate.description: channel-event (required): what the agent receives. Must not render empty.

inputMapping.description: start-flow: flow input → dot-path into the payload.

tools.name: automate_update-automation
tools.description: Change an automation: name, trigger, action and/or enabled. Trigger and action use the same shapes as create-automation and replace the previous ones; runtime state (counters, webhook token) is kept. Switching the trigger to webhook returns a new URL once.

action.description: New action (see create-automation).

tools.name: automate_enable-automation
tools.description: Enable (resume) an automation. Idempotent. A disabled schedule re-arms at its next cron slot.

tools.name: automate_disable-automation
tools.description: Disable (pause) an automation without deleting it. Idempotent. It keeps its configuration and history.

tools.name: automate_snooze-reminder
tools.description: Postpone a once automation (reminder) by a delay — "30m", "2h", "1d" — on top of its current time. Re-arms it if it already fired.

tools.name: automate_regenerate-webhook-url
tools.description: Rotate the secret URL of a webhook automation. The old URL stops working immediately; the new one is returned once.

tools.name: automate_test-webhook
tools.description: Fire a webhook automation with a test payload, exactly as an external POST would (dedupe, audit, stats). The action really runs.

payload.description: JSON object the action receives as {{payload}}.

tools.name: automate_delete-automation
tools.description: Permanently delete an automation. It stops firing immediately; tasks, messages and flow runs it already produced are kept. Irreversible.

tools.name: automate_cancel-reminder
tools.description: Cancel a pending reminder (once automation). Idempotent: an already fired or missing reminder returns noop.

tools.name: automate_bulk-cancel
tools.description: Delete several automations at once: by ids, or every automation that targets a channel, optionally only a trigger kind and only those whose next run is before an ISO date. Max 100 per call. Irreversible.

channelId.description: Every automation whose action targets this channel.

before.description: ISO date: only automations whose next run is before it.

tools.name: board-manager_-health-check
tools.description: Internal health check tool. Verifies WebSocket connectivity to backend.

tools.name: board-manager_-subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe this conversation to one of this app's events (task_created, task_moved, task_assigned, task_unassigned, task_started, task_completed, task_blocked, task_cancelled, task_updated, task_priority_changed, task_progress_note, task_archived, task_unarchived, task_dependency_added, task_dependency_removed, task_linked). Matching events are delivered here as they happen and wake the agent (self-wake guard: an agent is never woken by an event it caused itself). The subscription lives in the backend — it survives restarts of this app. Subscribing again to the same event REPLACES the previous filter. Returns: { subscription: { subscriptionId, topic, event, channelId, mode, filter, wakeUpOn, createdAt }, message }.

event.description: Local event name (the app namespace is implicit). Valid: task_created — A task was created on a board.; task_moved — A task changed column.; task_assigned — A task was assigned to an agent.; task_unassigned — A task lost its assignee.; task_started — An agent started working on a task.; task_completed — A task was completed.; task_blocked — A task was marked as blocked.; task_cancelled — A task was cancelled.; task_updated — A task field changed (title, description, instructions, tags, priority…).; task_priority_changed — A task priority changed.; task_progress_note — A progress note was added to a task.; task_archived — A task was archived.; task_unarchived — A task was restored from the archive.; task_dependency_added — A dependency was added between two tasks.; task_dependency_removed — A dependency was removed.; task_linked — A conversation was linked to a task (its context now lives in that channel).

filter.description: Optional filter. Fields AND-ed, values within a field OR-ed. Only the fields declared for the event are valid — see the event list.

wakeUpOn.description: Event names that wake the agent (response turn). Default: the subscribed event always wakes. Rarely needed with a single-event subscription.

channelId.description: Conversation that receives the events. Defaults to the calling conversation — omit it.

mode.description: notify = silent delivery, wake = trigger an agent response turn. Default: wake.

tools.name: board-manager_-unsubscribe
tools.description: Cancel this conversation's subscription(s) to this app's events. By subscriptionId, by event name, or — with neither — ALL of this conversation's subscriptions to this app. Idempotent. Returns: { unsubscribed, deleted?, channelId }.

event.description: Cancel the subscription to this event.

channelId.description: Defaults to the calling conversation.

tools.name: board-manager_-list-subscriptions
tools.description: List this conversation's subscriptions to this app's events, plus the app's event catalog (events, payload fields and valid filter fields) to subscribe to. Returns: { subscriptions: [...], events: [...] }.

channelId.description: Defaults to the calling conversation.

tools.name: board-manager_get-project
tools.description: Get project detail + its board columns. Returns: { project: { projectId, name, description, context, status, boardId, createdAt }, board: { boardId, columns: [{ columnId, slug, name, position }] } }. Use list-tasks to enumerate tasks.

tools.name: board-manager_list-projects
tools.description: List projects in a workspace. Returns: { workspaceId, projects: [{ projectId, name, description, status, boardId, taskCount, activeAgentCount, createdAt }], nextCursor? }. Paginated: default 50, max 200. Use get-project for full detail + board columns.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (optional, defaults to execution workspace)

tools.name: board-manager_get-task
tools.description: Get task detail + sub-tasks. Returns: { task: { taskId, title, description, columnName, columnSlug, priority, tags, assigneeName, running, stopRequested, dependencies, progressNotes, projectName, parentTaskTitle?, workflowInputData?, workflowOutputData?, workflowExecutionId?, workflowNodeId?, workflowInputGate?, workflowOutputGate? }, subTasks: [...], agents }. Workflow extension fields are present only when the task was created by the workflow engine.

fields.description: Custom subset of fields for task + subTasks

tools.name: board-manager_list-tasks
tools.description: List tasks in a project. Returns: { projectId, projectName, tasks: [{ taskId, title, columnName, columnSlug, priority, archived, tags, running, assigneeName, assigneeAvatarUrl }], agents, nextCursor? }. Paginated: default 50, max 200. For agent-view of own tasks use get-my-tasks (runner MCA).

tags.description: Return only tasks that have ALL these tags (optional)

archived.description: true=archived only, false=active only (default: active)

fields.description: Custom subset of fields to return (overrides default whitelist)

tools.name: board-manager_list-board-agents
tools.description: List agents in the workspace with access to board-manager or board-runner apps. Returns: { agents: [{ agentId, name, fullName, role, avatarUrl, capabilities }], nextCursor? }. Paginated: default 50, max 200.

workspaceId.description: Workspace (optional, defaults to execution)

tools.name: board-manager_create-project
tools.description: Create a project with an associated Kanban board in a workspace. Returns: { project: { projectId, workspaceId, name, status, boardId }, board: { boardId, columns: [...] } }. Default columns: Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Blocked, Review, Done.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (optional, defaults to execution workspace)

name.description: Project name

description.description: Optional project description

tools.name: board-manager_create-task
tools.description: Create a task on a project board. Defaults to Backlog column. Returns: { task: { taskId, title, columnId, priority, tags, assignedAgentId } }. Use batch-create-tasks to create many atomically. `instructions` is required — it gives the assigned agent the context and steps needed to work autonomously.

description.description: Short one-line summary of what the task is about (max ~1000 chars)

instructions.description: Detailed task instructions in markdown — context, specific steps, acceptance criteria, relevant paths, examples, and constraints. This is what the assigned agent receives as their briefing, so providing clear instructions is highly valuable for autonomous execution.

tools.name: board-manager_batch-create-tasks
tools.description: Create multiple tasks atomically (all succeed or all fail). Max 100 per call. Returns: { projectId, tasks: [{ taskId, title, columnId, priority, tags }], count }. Use create-task for a single task. `instructions` is required for each task — it gives the assigned agent the context and steps needed to work autonomously.

description.description: Short one-line summary of what the task is about (max ~1000 chars)

instructions.description: Detailed task instructions in markdown — context, specific steps, acceptance criteria, relevant paths, examples, and constraints. This is what the assigned agent receives as their briefing, so providing clear instructions is highly valuable for autonomous execution.

tools.name: board-manager_update-task
tools.description: Partial update of task properties. Omitted fields unchanged. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS } }. To move a task between columns use move-task. To assign an agent use assign-task.

description.description: New short one-line summary of what the task is about (max ~1000 chars)

instructions.description: New detailed task instructions in markdown — context, specific steps, acceptance criteria, relevant paths, examples, and constraints. This is what the assigned agent receives as their briefing, so providing clear instructions is highly valuable for autonomous execution.

tools.name: board-manager_archive-task
tools.description: Archive or restore a task (manager action). archived=true takes the task out of the active board (done / cancelled / discarded); archived=false restores it and triggers autoplay rescheduling. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS } }.

archived.description: true = archive, false = restore to active board

archiveNote.description: Optional note explaining why the task was archived

tools.name: board-manager_archive-project
tools.description: Archive a project (soft-delete) and all its non-archived tasks. Only admin/owner can archive. Idempotent — if already archived, returns the project. Returns: { project: { ...PROJECT_FIELDS } }.

archiveNote.description: Optional note explaining why the project was archived

tools.name: board-manager_update-project
tools.description: Partial update of project properties (name, description, context). context is injected into agent system prompts when working on this project (markdown supported). Returns: { project: { ...PROJECT_FIELDS } }.

name.description: New name

description.description: New description

context.description: Project context injected into agent system prompts (architecture notes, coding standards, etc.). Markdown supported.

tools.name: board-manager_update-board-config
tools.description: Update the board execution config for a project. The config object is passed as-is to the board. Currently reserved for future auto-dispatcher settings. Returns: { projectId, config }.

config.description: Board config object (passed as-is to the board document)

tools.name: board-manager_move-task
tools.description: Move a task to a different column on the board. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS } } (includes columnName + columnSlug after move). Use list-board-subscriptions + subscribe-to-board to get notified when tasks move.

position.description: Position within the column (optional, defaults to end)

reviewAction.description: Set true ONLY when this move is the terminal action of a review (verdict) while reacting to a task_moved→Review event. Enables the single-flight claim so concurrent sessions of yours move the task at most once. Leave unset for normal task management moves.

tools.name: board-manager_assign-task
tools.description: Assign or unassign an agent to a task. Pass agentId to assign, omit or null to unassign. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS } }.

agentId.description: Agent ID (omit or null to unassign)

tools.name: board-manager_start-task
tools.description: Start a task: moves to in_progress, creates a headless conversation with the assigned agent, sends the task description as the first message, and links the conversation to the task. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS, channelId }, channelId }. Optional override of agent or prompt.

agentId.description: Optional agent override. Reassigns the task before starting.

prompt.description: Optional custom prompt. Overrides the default task description as the first message.

tools.name: board-manager_link-conversation
tools.description: Link an existing conversation (channel) to a task. Replaces any previously linked channel. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS, channelId } }. Use start-task to link a new headless conversation instead.

channelId.description: Channel ID to link

tools.name: board-manager_add-progress-note
tools.description: Post a progress note on a task (manager action). Notes are visible on the task detail and the board. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_WITH_PROGRESS_FIELDS } }. Runner agents should use the board-runner add-progress-note instead.

reviewAction.description: Set true ONLY when this note is a review verdict posted while reacting to a task_moved→Review event. Enables the single-flight claim so concurrent sessions of yours post at most one review note. Leave unset for normal progress reporting.

tools.name: board-manager_delete-task
tools.description: Permanently delete a task. Sub-tasks become top-level tasks. Linked conversations are NOT deleted. Irreversible. Returns: { taskId, deleted: true }.

tools.name: board-manager_delete-project
tools.description: Permanently delete a project and all its tasks and board. Only workspace admin/owner can delete. Irreversible — prefer archive-project for soft-delete. Returns: { projectId, deleted: true }.

tools.name: board-manager_add-task-dependency
tools.description: Add a dependency: after this call, taskId depends on dependsOnTaskId (dependsOnTaskId must complete first). Cycle detection runs automatically; if adding the edge would create a cycle, the call errors and affected tasks are marked circular_dependency. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS, dependencies } }.

taskId.description: Task that gains the new dependency (the dependent task)

dependsOnTaskId.description: Task that taskId will depend on (must complete first)

tools.name: board-manager_remove-task-dependency
tools.description: Remove a dependency between two tasks. Idempotent — if the dependency does not exist, the task is returned unchanged. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS, dependencies } }.

taskId.description: Task that currently has the dependency

dependsOnTaskId.description: Task to remove from taskId's dependencies

tools.name: board-manager_get-task-dependencies
tools.description: Get dependencies of a task (tasks that must complete before it can start). Returns: { taskId, dependencies: [{ taskId, title, columnSlug, priority, archived }], count, nextCursor? }. Paginated when large: default 50, max 200.

taskId.description: Task ID whose dependencies to list

tools.name: board-manager_set-agent-slots
tools.description: Configure parallel execution slots for an agent in a project. slots=0 disables autoplay (also auto-disables playEnabled if it was on). slots≥1 enables the play button. Returns: { relationship: { agentId, projectId, slots, playEnabled, activeSlots } }. Use set-agent-play to toggle autoplay after setting slots.

agentId.description: Agent ID

slots.description: Parallel execution slots (0 = disabled, ≥1 = available)

tools.name: board-manager_set-agent-play
tools.description: Toggle autoplay for an agent on a project. When enabled=true the agent auto-picks eligible To Do tasks up to its slot limit. Requires slots≥1 (use set-agent-slots first). Disabling does NOT cancel tasks already running. Returns: { relationship: { agentId, projectId, slots, playEnabled } }.

agentId.description: Agent ID

tools.name: board-manager_subscribe-to-board
tools.description: DEPRECATED (v1.4.4): use the reserved tool `board_manager__subscribe` instead — one event per subscription with declarative filters (e.g. event "task_moved", filter { projectId, taskId, toColumn }); the subscription lives in the backend and survives respawns. This tool still works (kept for existing conversations) but will be removed. Subscribe the current conversation to real-time board events. Events (task moves, archives, assignments, progress notes, dependency changes, autoplay toggles) are delivered to the conversation as they happen. Use filter to narrow events. Returns: { subscription: { subscriptionId, boardId, filter, createdAt } }. Use unsubscribe-from-board to stop.

filter.description: Optional filter to narrow delivered events

agentIds.description: Only events for tasks assigned to these agents

columnIds.description: Only events for tasks in these columns

eventTypes.description: Valid: board.task_moved, board.task_archived, board.task_assigned, board.task_created, board.task_updated, board.task_progress_note, board.agent_play_changed, board.agent_slots_changed, board.dependency_added, board.dependency_removed

taskIds.description: Only events for these specific tasks (task IDs)

wakeUpOn.description: Event types that wake the agent (trigger a response turn). Default: ALL event types wake the agent (only a wakeUpOn list narrows it). Note: an agent is never woken by an event it caused itself (self-wake guard).

tools.name: board-manager_unsubscribe-from-board
tools.description: Cancel this conversation's subscription to board events for a specific board. Idempotent — if no subscription exists, returns { boardId, unsubscribed: true } unchanged. Returns: { boardId, unsubscribed: true }.

tools.name: board-manager_list-board-subscriptions
tools.description: List active board subscriptions for the current conversation. Returns: { subscriptions: [{ subscriptionId, boardId, boardName, filter, createdAt }], nextCursor? }. Paginated: default 50, max 200.

tools.name: board-manager_get-board-status
tools.description: Operational status of a board: per-agent workload + summary. Returns: { boardId, boardName, agents: [{ agentName, slots, playEnabled, activeSlots, activeTasks: [{ taskId, title, projectName }], tasksInProgress, tasksInReview, tasksBlocked, tasksToDo }], summary: { total, byColumn, blockedTasks } }. activeTasks lists the running tasks for each agent with activeSlots > 0. Use to identify bottlenecks.

tools.name: board-manager_stop-task
tools.description: Send cooperative stop signal to a running task (task.running=true). The assigned runner agent finishes its current step, then moves the task to Blocked. Cooperative — the signal is processed at the next runner turn. Only managers should call this. Returns: { taskId, stopRequested: true }.

taskId.description: Task ID of a running task

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason delivered to the runner

tools.name: board-manager_subscribe-to-events
tools.description: DEPRECATED (v1.4.4): use the reserved per-app tools instead — `board_manager__subscribe` for this app's events, `<app>__subscribe` for any other app's (e.g. gmail__subscribe with event "email.received"). The reserved tools take the LOCAL event name, validate filters against the app's declaration and keep state in the backend. This tool still works (raw topic + rules) but will be removed. Subscribe the current conversation to MCA events on a topic. Events matching the topic are delivered to the conversation as they happen. Use rules to narrow events. Returns: { subscription: { id, topic, channelId, rules, mode, createdAt } }. Use unsubscribe-from-events to stop.

topic.description: Event topic to subscribe to (e.g. "telegram.message.received")

channelId.description: Channel ID to receive events in (defaults to current conversation)

rules.description: Optional filter rules to narrow delivered events

mode.description: Delivery mode: notify = silent notification, wake = trigger agent response turn (the agent gets a response turn). Default: wake

tools.name: board-manager_unsubscribe-from-events
tools.description: Delete a channel event subscription by ID. Returns: { deleted: true }.

tools.name: board-manager_list-event-subscriptions
tools.description: List active event subscriptions for a channel. Returns: { subscriptions: [{ id, topic, channelId, rules, mode, createdAt, lastActivityAt }], nextCursor? }. Paginated: default 50, max 200.

channelId.description: Channel ID to list subscriptions for (defaults to current conversation)

tools.name: datetime_get-current
tools.description: Get current date and time in specified timezone. Returns a rich JSON with ISO, Unix timestamps, human-readable, weekday, etc. Optionally format with a custom format string.

timezone.description: Timezone (e.g., 'Europe/Madrid', 'America/New_York'). Defaults to local

format.description: Optional output format. Accepts Luxon tokens ('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') or Moment.js tokens ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'). If omitted, returns rich JSON.

tools.name: datetime_format
tools.description: Format a date/time string. Accepts ISO 8601, Unix timestamps (seconds or ms), and common formats. Supports both Luxon and Moment.js format tokens.

datetime.description: Date/time to format. Accepts: ISO 8601, Unix timestamp (seconds or ms, as string or number), RFC 2822, SQL, or common formats.

format.description: Output format. Luxon tokens ('yyyy-MM-dd', 'HH:mm:ss', 'cccc, d LLLL yyyy') or Moment.js tokens ('YYYY-MM-DD', 'dddd, D MMMM YYYY').

inputFormat.description: Explicit input format (Luxon tokens) if auto-detection fails (optional)

timezone.description: Target timezone for output (e.g., 'Europe/Madrid'). Defaults to keeping the input's timezone.

tools.name: datetime_parse
tools.description: Parse a date/time string into structured data. Accepts ISO 8601, Unix timestamps (seconds or ms), RFC 2822, SQL, and common formats. Returns rich JSON with all representations.

datetime.description: Date/time to parse. Accepts: ISO 8601, Unix timestamp (seconds or ms), RFC 2822, SQL, or common formats.

format.description: Explicit input format (Luxon tokens) if auto-detection fails (optional)

timezone.description: Target timezone for output (e.g., 'Europe/Madrid'). Defaults to keeping the input's timezone.

tools.name: datetime_convert-timezone
tools.description: Convert a date/time between timezones. Accepts ISO 8601, Unix timestamps, and common formats. Returns rich JSON for both source and target.

datetime.description: Date/time to convert. Accepts: ISO 8601, Unix timestamp (seconds or ms), RFC 2822, SQL, or common formats.

fromTimezone.description: Source timezone (e.g., 'Europe/Madrid'). If input is a Unix timestamp, this is ignored (always UTC).

tools.name: datetime_add
tools.description: Add duration to a date/time. Accepts ISO 8601, Unix timestamps, and common formats.

datetime.description: Base date/time. Accepts: ISO 8601, Unix timestamp (seconds or ms), RFC 2822, SQL, or common formats.

timezone.description: Timezone for output (e.g., 'Europe/Madrid'). Defaults to keeping the input's timezone.

tools.name: datetime_subtract
tools.description: Subtract duration from a date/time. Accepts ISO 8601, Unix timestamps, and common formats.

datetime.description: Base date/time. Accepts: ISO 8601, Unix timestamp (seconds or ms), RFC 2822, SQL, or common formats.

timezone.description: Timezone for output (e.g., 'Europe/Madrid'). Defaults to keeping the input's timezone.

tools.name: datetime_diff
tools.description: Calculate difference between two dates. Accepts ISO 8601, Unix timestamps, and common formats.

start.description: Start date/time. Accepts: ISO 8601, Unix timestamp, RFC 2822, SQL, or common formats.

end.description: End date/time. Accepts: ISO 8601, Unix timestamp, RFC 2822, SQL, or common formats.

tools.name: datetime_is-valid
tools.description: Validate a date/time string. Accepts ISO 8601, Unix timestamps, RFC 2822, SQL, and common formats. Returns whether it parses and what it parses to.

datetime.description: Date/time string to validate

format.description: Explicit input format (Luxon tokens) to test against (optional)

tools.name: conversations_-health-check
tools.description: Internal health check tool. Verifies WebSocket connectivity to backend.

tools.name: conversations_search-messages
tools.description: Search for text in messages across all past conversations. Returns matches grouped by channel with context snippets.

query.description: Text to search for (case-insensitive, minimum 2 characters)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50, max: 100)

tools.name: conversations_list-channels
tools.description: List past conversations. Returns channel names, agents, and last message preview.

status.description: Filter by channel status

limit.description: Maximum number of channels to return (default: 20)

tools.name: conversations_get-channel-messages
tools.description: Get messages from a specific past conversation. Supports pagination.

channelId.description: The ID of the channel to get messages from

before.description: Message ID for pagination - get messages before this one

textOnly.description: Only return text messages, excluding tool executions (default: true)

tools.name: conversations_get-channel-summary
tools.description: Get a quick summary of a conversation without all messages. Useful to understand what a conversation was about.

channelId.description: The ID of the channel to summarize

tools.name: conversations_create-conversation
tools.description: Create a new conversation with a specific agent. Returns the new channel ID that can be used to send messages.

agentId.description: The ID of the agent to start a conversation with

name.description: Optional name for the conversation

tools.name: conversations_delegate-task
tools.description: Delegate a task to a new sub-conversation with an agent (defaults to yourself). Creates the conversation, sends the task prompt, and returns immediately. The sub-agent works independently and each of its responses is automatically forwarded back to this conversation.

prompt.description: Full task description and instructions to send to the sub-agent

agentId.description: Agent ID to delegate to. Defaults to the current agent (self-delegation).

taskName.description: Optional name for the delegated task conversation

tools.name: conversations_send-message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing conversation. The agent will process and respond to the message.

channelId.description: The ID of the channel to send the message to

message.description: The message text to send

tools.name: conversations_rename-channel
tools.description: Rename a conversation. Changes the title/name of a channel. Without channelId it renames the current conversation. Conversations linked to a board task cannot be renamed — rename the task instead and the conversation follows.

channelId.description: The ID of the channel to rename. Optional — defaults to the current conversation.

name.description: The new name/title for the conversation

tools.name: conversations_import-attachment
tools.description: Copy a file the user uploaded in chat (image or document) into the agent workspace volume so filesystem tools can read it. Identify it by the filename shown in the "[User sent ...]" message reference. Returns { workspacePath, size, mime }.

filename.description: Filename of the chat attachment to import, as shown in the message reference

destPath.description: Optional destination path inside the workspace (relative). Defaults to the original filename at the workspace root.

channelId.description: Channel to import from. Defaults to the current conversation.

messageId.description: Optional message ID to disambiguate when several attachments share a filename.

overwrite.description: Overwrite the destination if it already exists (default: false).

tools.name: conversations_redact-by-value
tools.description: Redact every message in a conversation that contains a given secret value — the message where it was pasted, tool outputs like SSH/terminal logs that captured it, your own echoes, and even the arguments of this very call. Use it when a secret leaked into the conversation and you want no trace of it left in plaintext. The owner can still un-redact any message. Returns a coverage report (message ids + count) so you can verify nothing was missed. NEVER use this to hide non-secret content — it is a safety primitive for credentials.

value.description: The exact secret text to sweep for (minimum 4 characters). Every message containing it will be redacted.

channelId.description: The conversation to sweep (default: the current one). Only channels you have access to.

window.description: How many recent messages to scan (default 200, max 1000).

alsoRedact.description: Extra message ids to redact when the exact match misses them (split key, transformed value).

tools.name: board-runner_-health-check
tools.description:
Internal health check tool. Verifies WebSocket connectivity to backend.

IMPORTANT — Cooperative stop protocol:
At the start of every turn, check if the current task has stopRequested=true by calling get-my-task.
If stopRequested is true on your active task:
1. Finish only the current atomic step (do not start new work).
2. Add a progress note explaining where you left off.
3. Call block-my-task with a reason explaining where you stopped.
4. Do NOT continue with further tool calls after completing steps 1-3.

tools.name: board-runner_get-my-tasks
tools.description: List tasks assigned to this agent across all projects in the workspace. Returns: { agentId, tasks: [{ taskId, title, columnName, columnSlug, priority, projectName, running, stopRequested }], nextCursor? }. Paginated: default 50, max 200. Use get-my-task for the active task in the current conversation.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (optional, defaults to current workspace)

tags.description: Return only tasks that have ALL these tags (optional). Useful for a cycle/release scope (e.g. ["cycle:sesion-20260412"]).

tools.name: board-runner_get-my-task
tools.description: Get the task linked to the current conversation (fast path). Returns: { channelId, task: { taskId, title, description, instructions, columnName, columnSlug, running, stopRequested, projectName, progressNotes, input, output } | null }. Check stopRequested at every turn; if true, finish current step, add a progress note, call block-my-task, and stop.

tools.name: board-runner_complete-my-task
tools.description: Mark your assigned task complete. Moves it to Review (ready for manager review). Works from any column including Blocked. Clears the running flag. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_FIELDS, columnSlug: "review" } }. If the task was created by a workflow, pass outputData with the artifact data produced by the task — it will be saved to workflowOutputData before the workflow engine advances.

outputData.description: Optional output data produced by the task (the deliverable). When the task is linked to a workflow execution, this data is validated against the output gate artifact schema before the workflow advances. Omit for non-workflow tasks.

tools.name: board-runner_block-my-task
tools.description: Mark your assigned task blocked. Moves it to Blocked + adds a progress note with the reason. Clears running. Use for dependencies, missing info, or external blockers. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_WITH_PROGRESS_FIELDS, columnSlug: "blocked" } }.

reason.description: Why the task is blocked (added as a progress note)

tools.name: board-runner_cancel-my-task
tools.description: Cancel your assigned task. Archives in-place (does not move column) + adds a progress note with the reason. Clears running. Use when the task is no longer needed, is a duplicate, or cannot be completed. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_WITH_PROGRESS_FIELDS, archived: true } }.

reason.description: Why the task is cancelled (added as a progress note)

tools.name: board-runner_add-progress-note
tools.description: Add a progress note to one of your assigned tasks. Notes are visible on the task detail and the board. Prefix with "PROPUESTA: " to suggest new tasks to the manager. Returns: { task: { ...TASK_WITH_PROGRESS_FIELDS } }.

reviewAction.description: Set true ONLY when this note is a review verdict posted while reacting to a task_moved→Review event. Enables the single-flight claim so concurrent sessions of yours post at most one review note. Leave unset for normal progress reporting.

tools.name: guide_-health-check
tools.description: Internal health check. Verifies the platform guide content is loaded.

tools.name: guide_list-guide-topics
tools.description: Index of the Teros platform guide (sections + one-line summaries). Teros UI, windows and exact steps are NOT in your training data — answering how-to questions about Teros from memory is usually wrong. Whenever the user asks how to do anything in Teros (create an agent, connect an app, set up a board, providers, files…), call this FIRST, then get-guide-section, and answer from the guide. Returns {topics:[{id,title,summary}], count}.

tools.name: guide_search-guide
tools.description: Search the Teros platform guide by free-text query and get the most relevant section(s) with a snippet — the fastest way to answer how-to questions about Teros. Teros specifics are NOT in your training data; search here instead of guessing. Returns {query, results:[{id,title,summary,score,snippet}], count}. Use get-guide-section for a result's full body.

query.description: Free-text query, e.g. "how do I create an agent" or "connect gmail".

tools.name: guide_get-guide-section
tools.description: Get one Teros platform-guide section by topic id (from list-guide-topics). Use this to answer how-to questions about Teros instead of guessing — Teros specifics are not in your training data. Returns {id,title,summary,body(markdown),related}. Read the body and walk the user through the real steps in their own language; do not paste it verbatim.

topic.description: Topic id to fetch. Must be one of the ids returned by `list-guide-topics`.

tools.name: email_-health-check
tools.description: Internal health check. Verifies transport configuration (mode, which secrets are present — never their values) and, when MAIL_ACCOUNT is configured, a live JMAP session with the derived or explicit password.

tools.name: email_session-info
tools.description: Identity of this email instance: mailbox (MAIL_ACCOUNT), JMAP accountId, username, apiUrl, transport mode and password source (derived/user). First call to diagnose connection or credentials.

tools.name: email_list-folders
tools.description: Folders of this mailbox (Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Trash, …) with role, total emails and unread count. Use the returned roles as 'folder' in list-messages.

tools.name: email_list-messages
tools.description: List messages of a folder, most recent first, without bodies (use read-message for the content). Returns { total, offset, messages: [{ id, from, to, subject, receivedAt, seen, flagged, draft, size }] }.

folder.description: Role ('inbox', 'sent', 'drafts', 'trash', 'junk') or exact folder name. Default 'inbox'.

tools.name: email_read-message
tools.description: Read a message in full: headers (from/to/cc/replyTo), subject, date and body (text and HTML when present). Does not change the read state (that is mark-read).

messageId.description: Email id (the one returned by list-messages).

tools.name: email_send
tools.description: Send an email from this instance's mailbox (the sender is ALWAYS the configured MAIL_ACCOUNT — never a tool parameter). Draft + submit in one JMAP request; the message is stored in Sent. Confirm with the user before sending to external recipients.

to.description: Recipient address or list of addresses.

html.description: Optional HTML body (alternative text/html part).

fromName.description: Display name of the sender. Default: MAIL_FROM_NAME, else the JMAP identity name.

tools.name: email_mark-read
tools.description: Mark messages as read or unread. Accepts a list (1..100) so a single confirmation covers the batch. Returns { updated, notUpdated }.

tools.name: email_destroy
tools.description: DESTROY messages permanently — irreversible, they do NOT pass through Trash. Use only with explicit user confirmation. Returns { destroyed, notDestroyed }.

tools.description: Internal health check tool. Verifies API keys and connectivity.

tools.name: file-processor_file-to-markdown
tools.description: Convert a file to text/Markdown (synchronous). Best for DIGITAL documents: PDFs with a real text layer and Word .docx are extracted exactly and instantly. For scans, photos, handwriting, stamps or ID cards, if you can see images use pdf-to-images instead and read the pages yourself — local OCR (used here as a fallback) is slower and less reliable. Use file-to-markdown-async for long-running jobs.

inputPath.description: Path to the file to convert

outputPath.description: Optional output path (defaults to input path with .md extension)

chunkSize.description: Pages per chunk for large PDFs (default: 10). Only used for PDFs >3MB

maxRetries.description: Maximum retries per chunk if processing fails (default: 3)

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds per chunk (default: 120000 for chunks, 180000 for direct processing)

tools.name: file-processor_file-to-markdown-async
tools.description: Convert a file to Markdown asynchronously (non-blocking). Supports PDF, Word .docx, and images (png/jpg/tiff/webp/gif/bmp). Returns a job ID immediately. Use get-job-status to check progress. For scans/photos/handwriting prefer pdf-to-images if you can see images.

inputPath.description: Path to the file to convert

outputPath.description: Optional output path (defaults to input path with .md extension)

chunkSize.description: Pages per chunk for large PDFs (default: 10)

maxRetries.description: Maximum retries per chunk if processing fails (default: 3)

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds per chunk (default: 120000)

tools.name: file-processor_get-job-status
tools.description: Get the status of an async job. Returns current progress, status, and results when completed.

jobId.description: The job ID returned by file-to-markdown-async

tools.name: file-processor_list-jobs
tools.description: List all jobs with optional filters. Useful for checking active jobs or recent completions.

status.description: Filter by status: queued, processing, completed, failed, cancelled

limit.description: Maximum number of jobs to return (default: 20)

tools.name: file-processor_cancel-job
tools.description: Cancel a queued or processing job. Cannot cancel completed/failed jobs.

jobId.description: The job ID to cancel

tools.name: file-processor_audio-to-text
tools.description: Transcribe audio files to text using OpenAI Whisper API. Supports .m4a, .mp3, .wav, .ogg, .webm, .opus and other audio formats.

inputPath.description: Path to the audio file to transcribe

language.description: Optional: Language code (e.g., 'es' for Spanish, 'en' for English). Defaults to 'es' (Spanish) to prevent auto-detection from misidentifying Spanish as Catalan/Galician/Portuguese.

tools.name: file-processor_svg-to-png
tools.description: Convert SVG files to PNG with optional width/height constraints

inputPath.description: Path to the SVG file to convert

outputPath.description: Optional output path (defaults to input path with .png extension)

tools.name: file-processor_ocr-extract
tools.description: FALLBACK ONLY — local OCR (tesseract.js) of an image or PDF. If you can see images, use pdf-to-images instead: reading the pages with vision is faster and far more accurate on scans, handwriting, pen corrections and stamps. Use this only when images are reported as not shown (model without vision). Returns per-page confidence scores and low-confidence word markers. Supports: png, jpg, jpeg, tiff, webp, gif, bmp, pdf.

inputPath.description: Path to the image or PDF file

pages.description: Pages to process, e.g. '1-3,5' (default: all). Only for PDFs.

format.description: Output format (default: 'markdown')

tools.name: file-processor_pdf-to-images
tools.description: Show a PDF or an image file to YOU (the model) as images in your context, so you can read it with vision — scans, handwriting, pen corrections, stamps, ID cards, forms. Each PDF page is rendered in colour and attached to the result like an image the user pasted in chat. Use it whenever you need to actually look at a document (e.g. a PDF downloaded from an email); prefer it over ocr-extract when you can see images, and fall back to ocr-extract if the images are reported as not shown. Supports pdf, png, jpg, jpeg, webp, gif, tiff, bmp. Max 10 pages per call — use `pages` for the rest.

inputPath.description: Path to the PDF or image file (e.g. /workspace/inbox/acta.pdf)

pages.description: PDF pages to show, e.g. '1-3,5' (default: the first 10). Ignored for images.

dpi.description: PDF render resolution (default 150; 200 for small print). Ignored for images.

maxDimension.description: Longest side of each attached image in px (default 1568, 512–2048).

autoRotate.description: Straighten sideways/upside-down pages (scanned IDs…) before attaching them (default true). Upright pages cost one quick check; only rotated ones take longer.

tools.name: todo-list_-health-check
tools.description: Internal health check. Verifies MongoDB connectivity.

tools.name: todo-list_add-node
tools.description: Add a new node to the tree. If parentId is omitted or null, adds as a root-level node. If parentId is provided, it must be an existing node ID — a wrong or truncated parentId returns "Parent node not found" and no node is created. kind "task" (default) is completable and has a state (default "planning" — an idea not yet ready; pass "pending" when the task is ready to start); kind "group" is a non-completable container (Home, Work…) with no state. A task cannot contain groups (GROUP_IN_TASK). Returns: { node: { nodeId, parentId, text, description, instructions, kind, state, blockedReason, reportedProgress, completed, collapsed, position, createdAt, updatedAt }, parentText: string | null } — node.nodeId is the complete ID of the created node.

parentId.description: Parent node ID to nest under — must exist (error if not found). Omit or null for a root-level node.

description.description: Short description under the title. Max 2000 chars.

instructions.description: Detailed markdown instructions for what to do with this task. Max 10000 chars.

kind.description: task (default, completable) or group (container without state). A group cannot go inside a task.

state.description: Initial state of a task (default planning — an idea not yet ready; pass pending when the task is ready to start). Not for groups. To block a task use set-state with a reason.

expectedOutput.description: Output the task must deliver: { format: "markdown"|"form"|"file", description?, fileType? (file only: pdf|docx|xlsx|csv|png|jpg|json|md|txt|html|other), fields? (form only: 1–40 fields [{ id, type: text|textarea|number|select|radio|checkbox|date|time|datetime, label, required?, options? }]) }. null clears it. set-output rejects an output that does not match it (OUTPUT_MISMATCH). Not for groups.

format.description: Format of the output.

description.description: What the output must contain. Max 500 chars.

fileType.description: format=file only: the exact file type (other = any file).

fields.description: format=form only: the fields the output form must have (1–40). A form output must carry every required field and no field outside this list.

tools.name: todo-list_get-node
tools.description: Get full detail of a single node, including instructions and the complete log. Use this when you need the full content of a task (get-tree only returns lightweight fields). Returns: { node: { nodeId, parentId, text, description, instructions, kind, state, blockedReason, allowedTransitions, progress, reportedProgress, input, output, hasInput, hasOutput, expectedOutput, completed, collapsed, position, log: [{ timestamp, text, actor }], createdAt, updatedAt } }. actor is who wrote the log entry ({ kind: user|agent|system, id? }), missing on older entries. progress is the effective % (reported, else 100 for review/done, else derived from the children); input/output are { format: markdown|form|file, ... } or null (a file carries objectId, url, name, mime, size); expectedOutput is the output the task must deliver ({ format, description?, fileType?, fields? }) or null.

tools.name: todo-list_get-tree
tools.description: Get the tree of nodes for the current user as a nested hierarchy (Workflowy-style). Returns: { tree: [{ nodeId, parentId, text, description, kind, state, blockedReason, completed, collapsed, position, progress, reportedProgress, hasInput, hasOutput, childCount, completedChildren, children?: [...] }] } — kind is task|group (groups have state null), progress is the effective % (reported, else 100 for review/done, else derived from the children). Pass nodeId to get only the subtree rooted at that node. Pass depth=0 to get only root-level nodes without children (lazy loading — each node still reports childCount/completedChildren so the UI can show expand arrows). depth=-1 (default) returns the full nested tree. depth=N returns N levels of children. Tree nodes do NOT include instructions or log — use get-node for full detail.

nodeId.description: Optional: get only the subtree rooted at this node.

depth.description: Tree depth to return. -1 = full tree (default), 0 = root level only (no children), N = N levels of children. Use 0 for lazy loading to keep responses small.

tools.name: todo-list_update-node
tools.description: Update the text, description, instructions and/or expected output definition of a node. Omitted fields are unchanged. Returns: { node: { nodeId, text, description, instructions, expectedOutput, updatedAt } }.

description.description: New short description. Max 2000 chars. Pass empty string to clear.

instructions.description: New detailed markdown instructions. Max 10000 chars. Pass empty string to clear.

expectedOutput.description: Output the task must deliver: { format: "markdown"|"form"|"file", description?, fileType? (file only: pdf|docx|xlsx|csv|png|jpg|json|md|txt|html|other), fields? (form only: 1–40 fields [{ id, type: text|textarea|number|select|radio|checkbox|date|time|datetime, label, required?, options? }]) }. null clears it. set-output rejects an output that does not match it (OUTPUT_MISMATCH). Not for groups.

format.description: Format of the output.

description.description: What the output must contain. Max 500 chars.

fileType.description: format=file only: the exact file type (other = any file).

fields.description: format=form only: the fields the output form must have (1–40). A form output must carry every required field and no field outside this list.

tools.name: todo-list_toggle-complete
tools.description: Toggle the completed state of a task: a task that is not done becomes done (100%), a done task goes back to pending. Cascades to all descendants — marking a parent complete also marks all children complete, and vice versa. Adds a log entry automatically. Groups cannot be completed (NOT_A_TASK). For any other state change use set-state. Returns: { node: { nodeId, state, reportedProgress, completed, updatedAt } }.

nodeId.description: Node ID to toggle completion on.

tools.name: todo-list_toggle-collapse
tools.description: Toggle the collapsed/expanded state of a node (hide/show children in Workflowy). Returns: { node: { nodeId, collapsed, updatedAt } }.

nodeId.description: Node ID to toggle collapse on.

tools.name: todo-list_move-node
tools.description: Move a node to a different parent and/or position within the tree. newParentId must be an existing node ID — a wrong or truncated ID returns "Parent node not found" and nothing is moved. Omit newParentId to keep the current parent and only reorder among siblings; set it explicitly to null to move to root level. newPosition is the 0-based index among siblings. Detects circular moves (cannot move a node into itself or its own subtree). Returns: { node: { nodeId, parentId, position, updatedAt } }.

newParentId.description: New parent node ID — must exist (error if not found). Omit to keep the current parent (reorder only). Set explicitly to null to move to root (top-level).

tools.name: todo-list_delete-node
tools.description: Delete a node and ALL its descendants (entire subtree). Irreversible. Returns: { deleted: true, node: { text, description, ... } }.

nodeId.description: Node ID to delete. All children will be removed recursively.

tools.name: todo-list_search-nodes
tools.description: Search nodes by text across all of the user's nodes. Case-insensitive. Returns: { results: [{ nodeId, text, description, completed, path, updatedAt }] } where path is a breadcrumb like "Parent / Child / Match". Max 50 results.

query.description: Search text (case-insensitive). Min 1 char, max 500.

tools.name: todo-list_add-log-entry
tools.description: Add a chronological log entry to a node. Used to track progress, notes, and history over time. Returns: { node: { nodeId, log: [{ timestamp, text }], updatedAt } }.

nodeId.description: Node ID to add the log entry to.

text.description: The log entry text. Max 2000 chars.

tools.name: todo-list_set-state
tools.description: Move a task to another state: planning (idea, not defined yet) · pending (defined, ready to start) · working (started) · blocked (cannot continue — reason required) · review (work finished, awaiting a check) · done · cancelled (this task is no longer happening — from any open state). Allowed moves: planning→pending|cancelled; pending→working|done|planning|cancelled; working→review|blocked|pending|done|cancelled; blocked→working|planning|cancelled; review→done|working|cancelled; done→working (reopen — give a reason); cancelled→pending (reopen). Anything else fails with INVALID_TRANSITION. Entering review or done sets progress to 100; leaving them for an open state clears a 100 (any other value is kept). Cancelling removes the task from the day plan and clears its progress; a cancelled task is ignored by autoplay and does not count for its parent's derived progress. Groups have no state (NOT_A_TASK). Adds a log entry "from → to". Returns: { node: { nodeId, parentId, text, kind, state, blockedReason, reportedProgress, completed, hasInput, hasOutput, updatedAt, ... }, transition: { from, to } }.

state.description: Target state.

reason.description: Why. Required for blocked (what is missing / who it waits for — shown to the user). Recommended when reopening a done task. Max 2000 chars.

reply.description: Only for blocked → working (the answer to the blocked question, logged as "Reply: <text>") or review → working (why the task is sent back, logged as "Sent back: <text>"). When the task has a conversation it is posted there (a send-back as "Sent back from review: <text>") and its agent continues. Max 2000 chars.

tools.name: todo-list_set-kind
tools.description: Convert a node between task and group, keeping its children. A group is a non-completable container (no state, progress or output); a task can be completed and contains only tasks. To group: fails with GROUP_IN_TASK if its parent is a task and HAS_OUTPUT if it has an output. To task: fails with GROUP_IN_TASK if it contains groups; it starts pending. Adds a log entry. Returns: { node: { nodeId, parentId, text, kind, state, ... } }.

kind.description: Target kind.

tools.name: todo-list_set-progress
tools.description: Report how far a task is, as an integer percentage 0–100, or null to clear it (the progress is then 100 for a task in review/done, else derived from its children). Editable in every state, review and done included; groups have no progress (NOT_A_TASK). Adds a log entry. Returns: { node: { nodeId, reportedProgress, state, ... } }.

tools.name: todo-list_set-input
tools.description: Set the input of a node — the data the task starts from — or clear it with null. Markdown and forms are stored on the node; a file arrives either as base64 data or as a path inside the workspace volume (the backend reads and uploads it) and is stored as { format: "file", objectId, url, name, mime, size }. Groups may hold input. Replacing an existing input that would actually change requires overwrite: true (OUTPUT_EXISTS otherwise); re-delivering the same thing is a no-op. Adds a log entry. Returns: { node: { nodeId, hasInput, input, ... } }.

input.description: One of: { format: "markdown", markdown } · { format: "form", fields: [{ id, type: text|textarea|number|select|radio|checkbox|date|time|datetime, label, options? }], values: { [fieldId]: value } } · { format: "file", path: "/workspace/..." (absolute path inside the workspace volume — the backend reads and uploads the file; name/mime optional, inferred from the filename) } · { format: "file", name, mime, data: base64 (max 10 MB, no data: prefix) — for in-memory files }. null clears it. Prefer path for any file that already exists in the workspace volume.

values.description: format=form: values keyed by field id.

name.description: format=file: file name. Optional with path (inferred from the filename); required with data.

mime.description: format=file: MIME type. Optional with path (inferred from the extension); required with data.

data.description: format=file: base64 content (max 10 MB decoded). In-memory files only — use path when the file exists in the workspace volume.

path.description: format=file: absolute path inside the workspace volume, e.g. "/workspace/report.html". The backend reads the file and uploads it — never generate base64 for a file that already exists on the volume.

overwrite.description: Set true to replace an existing input. Required when the node already has an input and the new one would change it.

tools.name: todo-list_set-output
tools.description: Deliver the output of a task — its result (a summary in markdown, a filled form, or a file such as an invoice) — or clear it with null. A file arrives either as base64 data or as a path inside the workspace volume (the backend reads and uploads it) and is stored as { format: "file", objectId, url, name, mime, size }. Groups have no output (NOT_A_TASK). Adds a log entry "Output delivered · <format>". When the task has an expectedOutput (see get-node), the output must match it — same format, the expected file type, every required form field and no field outside the definition — or it fails with OUTPUT_MISMATCH. Replacing an existing output that would actually change requires overwrite: true (OUTPUT_EXISTS otherwise); re-delivering the same thing is a no-op. Delivering does not change the state: use set-state (e.g. working → review) as well. Returns: { node: { nodeId, hasOutput, output, ... } }.

output.description: One of: { format: "markdown", markdown } · { format: "form", fields: [{ id, type: text|textarea|number|select|radio|checkbox|date|time|datetime, label, options? }], values: { [fieldId]: value } } · { format: "file", path: "/workspace/..." (absolute path inside the workspace volume — the backend reads and uploads the file; name/mime optional, inferred from the filename) } · { format: "file", name, mime, data: base64 (max 10 MB, no data: prefix) — for in-memory files }. null clears it. Prefer path for any file that already exists in the workspace volume.

values.description: format=form: values keyed by field id.

name.description: format=file: file name. Optional with path (inferred from the filename); required with data.

mime.description: format=file: MIME type. Optional with path (inferred from the extension); required with data.

data.description: format=file: base64 content (max 10 MB decoded). In-memory files only — use path when the file exists in the workspace volume.

path.description: format=file: absolute path inside the workspace volume, e.g. "/workspace/report.html". The backend reads the file and uploads it — never generate base64 for a file that already exists on the volume.

overwrite.description: Set true to replace an existing output. Required when the task already has an output and the new one would change it (e.g. a different file or different markdown).

tools.name: todo-list_toggle-instruction-item
tools.description: Tick or untick one checklist item of a node's instructions — the index-th (0-based) markdown checkbox line ("- [ ] step" / "- [x] step"), counting top to bottom and ignoring code blocks. Fails with ITEM_NOT_FOUND past the last item. Returns: { node: { nodeId, parentId, instructions, updatedAt }, item: { index, checked, text } }.

index.description: 0-based index of the checkbox among all checkboxes of the instructions.

tools.name: todo-list_plan-node
tools.description: Plan a task for a calendar day ("Por día"), reorder it within its day, set its time, or take it off its day. day is "YYYY-MM-DD" in the user's calendar, or null to remove it from its day (also clears the time). index places it in the day's plan (0 = first; omitted = end of the day, or its current slot when the day does not change); the day is renumbered 0..N-1. time "HH:MM" sets the planned time, null clears it, omitted keeps it. Groups are never planned (NOT_A_TASK). Logs "Planned for <day>", "Planned time …" or "Removed from the day". Returns: { node: { nodeId, plannedFor, dayOrder, plannedTime, state, ... }, day, previousDay }.

day.description: Day "YYYY-MM-DD", or null to remove the task from its day.

index.description: Position in the day's plan (0-based). Optional.

time.description: Planned time "HH:MM" (24 h), or null to clear it. Optional.

tools.name: todo-list_get-day
tools.description: Get one day of the plan: the tasks planned for day in plan order, the overdue tasks (open tasks planned before today, oldest first) and the unplanned open tasks (no day, tree order). Pass today as the user's current calendar day "YYYY-MM-DD" (defaults to the UTC date). Returns: { day, today, tasks: [...], overdue: [...], unplanned: [...] } where each task is { nodeId, parentId, text, state, blockedReason, progress, reportedProgress, plannedFor, dayOrder, plannedTime, hasOutput, path: [ancestor titles, root first] }.

day.description: Day "YYYY-MM-DD".

today.description: The user's current day "YYYY-MM-DD" (decides what is overdue). Optional.

tools.name: todo-list_assign-node
tools.description: Assign a task to an agent or a person of the workspace ("who does what"), or unassign it with null. assignee is { kind: "agent" | "user", id } — an agentId usable in this workspace or the userId of a workspace member (owner included); anything else fails with INVALID_ASSIGNEE. Groups cannot be assigned (NOT_A_TASK). Stores assignedAt and logs "Assigned to <name>" / "Unassigned". Assigning does not start the task. Returns: { node: { nodeId, assignee, assignedAt, state, ... } }.

assignee.description: Who does it, or null to unassign.

kind.description: An agent or a human member.

tools.name: todo-list_set-reviewer
tools.description: Set the reviewer of a task — who reviews it when it enters review — or clear it with null (back to manual validation — nobody evaluates, the default). reviewer is { kind: "agent" | "user", id } — an agentId usable in this workspace or the userId of a workspace member; anything else fails with INVALID_ASSIGNEE. Groups cannot be reviewed (NOT_A_TASK). Empty by default: a task without a reviewer behaves exactly as before. When a task WITH a reviewer enters review, the reviewer is notified automatically and the task shows in their view — no subscription needed. Logs "Reviewer set to <name>" / "Reviewer removed". Returns: { node: { nodeId, reviewer, reviewedAt, state, ... } }.

reviewer.description: Who reviews it, or null to clear (manual validation — nobody evaluates).

kind.description: An agent or a human member.

tools.name: todo-list_add-dependency
tools.description: Make a task wait on another task of the same workspace (any group - never cross-workspace): while the blocker is unresolved the task is NOT started by the autoplay, and the day/tree rows show it with the waiting semaforo. A dependency releases when the blocker reaches done or cancelled - review does NOT release (board parity). Groups can neither wait nor block (NOT_A_TASK); a blocker from another workspace is not found; self, direct and transitive cycles fail with CIRCULAR_DEPENDENCY. Adding an existing dependency is a no-op (added: false). Logs "Depends on <title>". Returns: { node: { nodeId, dependencies, ... }, dependency: { nodeId, text, state }, added: boolean }.

nodeId.description: Task node ID - the task that waits.

blockerNodeId.description: Task node ID - the task it waits on (the blocker).

tools.name: todo-list_remove-dependency
tools.description: Remove a dependency: the task stops waiting on the blocker and becomes autoplay-eligible again at once (the scheduling triggers run). Removing one that is not there is a no-op (removed: false). Groups have no dependencies (NOT_A_TASK). Logs "Dependency removed: <title>". Returns: { node: { nodeId, dependencies, ... }, dependency: { nodeId, text, state } | null, removed: boolean }.

nodeId.description: Task node ID - the task that waits.

blockerNodeId.description: Task node ID - the blocker it stops waiting on.

tools.name: todo-list_get-autoplay
tools.description: List the Tasks autoplay runners of this workspace and its global state: the agents that pick up their own tasks (pending and planned for today or earlier) with a number of parallel slots. activeSlots is how many of the agent's tasks are running now; globalPlaying is the workspace's autoplay play/pause (TODOAP-REQ-30); runningCount is how many todo tasks of the workspace have a live turn — the STOP control's visibility (TODOAP-REQ-31). Returns: { globalPlaying: boolean, runningCount: number, runners: [{ agentId, name, avatarUrl, slots, playEnabled, activeSlots, scopeNodeId, scopePath, pickUnassigned, scopeMissing }] }.

tools.name: todo-list_set-agent-slots
tools.description: Set how many tasks an agent of this workspace runs in parallel (makes it a runner if it is not one). 0 slots also pauses it. The agent must belong to the workspace (INVALID_ASSIGNEE). Read members cannot change runners (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { runner: { agentId, name, avatarUrl, slots, playEnabled, activeSlots, scopeNodeId, scopePath, pickUnassigned, scopeMissing } }.

agentId.description: Agent ID.

slots.description: Parallel executions (0 = listed but cannot run).

tools.name: todo-list_set-agent-play
tools.description: Turn autoplay on or off for an agent (makes it a runner if it is not one). With play on, Teros starts the agent's pending tasks planned for today or earlier, honouring its slots. Enabling with 0 slots fails with INVALID_STATE. Pausing never interrupts a running turn. Read members cannot change runners (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { runner: { agentId, name, avatarUrl, slots, playEnabled, activeSlots, scopeNodeId, scopePath, pickUnassigned, scopeMissing } }.

agentId.description: Agent ID.

tools.name: todo-list_set-global-play
tools.description: Set the workspace's global autoplay play/pause — the Tasks panel's Play/Pause control. Playing starts ONLY the enabled runners (playEnabled true with slots); a disabled runner is excluded from the global control. Pausing stops every scheduler path but never interrupts running turns. Read members cannot change it (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { globalPlaying: boolean }.

playing.description: true = the workspace's autoplay plays, false = paused.

tools.name: todo-list_stop-autoplay
tools.description: The workspace's global STOP: pause the autoplay AND abort every in-flight turn of the workspace's todo tasks — the equivalent of going to each task's conversation and pressing stop. The tasks stay working with no live turn; nothing restarts until the global play. Read members cannot stop (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { globalPlaying: false, aborted: number of turns aborted }.

tools.name: todo-list_set-agent-scope
tools.description: Set an agent runner's scope (makes it a runner if it is not one). With pickUnassigned true, the agent also picks up tasks with no assignee that are pending and planned for today or earlier, inside the scope group (any depth; the whole tree when scopeNodeId is null), after its own tasks; each one is assigned to the agent before it starts. Tasks assigned to the agent are picked wherever they are. scopeNodeId must be a group of this workspace (INVALID_INPUT). Read members cannot change runners (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { runner: { agentId, name, avatarUrl, slots, playEnabled, activeSlots, scopeNodeId, scopePath, pickUnassigned, scopeMissing } }.

agentId.description: Agent ID.

scopeNodeId.description: Group node ID that bounds the unassigned pickup, or null for the whole tree.

pickUnassigned.description: true = also pick up unassigned planned tasks inside the scope.

tools.name: todo-list_remove-agent
tools.description: Remove an agent from the autoplay runners. Its running turns are not interrupted and its tasks keep their conversations. Read members cannot change runners (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { removed: true, agentId }.

agentId.description: Agent ID.

tools.name: todo-list_start-node
tools.description: Start a task now: for a task assigned to an agent that is pending (or working without a conversation), whatever its planned day and the runner's play/slots. Moves it to working, opens (or reuses) its conversation with the agent and sends the agent the task. Not assigned to an agent: NOT_AGENT_TASK; any other state: INVALID_STATE. Returns: { node: { nodeId, state, channelId, running, ... }, channelId }.

tools.name: todo-list_open-runner-terminal
tools.description: Open the task's work context (CCR-REQ-8): reveal the runner's terminal in the Terminal window, or recreate it with `claude --resume <sessionId>` when the session is gone — Claude Code recovers its full memory of the task. Idempotent: an alive terminal is only revealed. No runner record: NOT_RUNNER_TASK (409); runner not wired: UNAVAILABLE (503). Returns: { terminalId, resumed, node }.

tools.name: todo-list_subscribe-to-todo
tools.description: DEPRECATED (v1.4.4): use the reserved tool `todo_list__subscribe` instead — one event per subscription with declarative filters (e.g. event "task_completed", filter { nodeId }); the subscription lives in the backend and survives respawns. This tool still works (kept for existing conversations) but will be removed. Subscribe this conversation to the to-do events of the workspace (task started, completed, blocked, assigned, planned, output delivered, progress, autoplay changes). Events that pass the filter are delivered here as they happen and wake the agent. Key use: filter.nodeIds + eventTypes ["task_completed"] = "avísame cuando ESTA tarea termine". The same events exist as todo.* topics for Automate. Upsert: subscribing again REPLACES the previous filter. Returns: { subscription: { subscriptionId, workspaceId, channelId, agentId, filter, createdAt, updatedAt }, created, message }.

channelId.description: Conversation that receives the events. Defaults to the calling agent's conversation — omit it when subscribing from the conversation that wants the events.

filter.description: Optional filter to narrow delivered events. Multiple fields are AND-ed; multiple values within a field are OR-ed. Empty = all events of the workspace.

nodeIds.description: Only events for these specific tasks (node IDs) — "avísame cuando ESTA tarea acabe".

assigneeIds.description: Only events where the task is assigned to one of these agents/users (ids).

states.description: Only events where the task's NEW state is one of these (planning, pending, working, blocked, review, done, cancelled).

groupNodeIds.description: Only events for tasks inside these groups' subtrees (group node IDs).

eventTypes.description: Only these event types. Valid: task_created, task_started, task_completed, task_blocked, task_state_changed, task_assigned, task_unassigned, task_planned, task_output_delivered, task_progress, task_updated, task_moved, task_deleted, agent_play_changed, agent_slots_changed.

wakeUpOn.description: Event types that wake the agent (trigger a response turn). Default: ALL event types wake the agent (only a wakeUpOn list narrows it). An agent is never woken by an event it caused itself (self-wake guard).

tools.name: todo-list_unsubscribe-from-todo
tools.description: Cancel this conversation's subscription to the workspace's to-do events. Idempotent — a subscription that does not exist returns { unsubscribed: true } unchanged. Returns: { unsubscribed: true, channelId, deleted }.

channelId.description: Conversation whose subscription to cancel. Defaults to the calling agent's conversation.

tools.name: todo-list_list-todo-subscriptions
tools.description: List this conversation's to-do event subscriptions in the workspace: { subscriptions: [{ subscriptionId, workspaceId, channelId, agentId, filter, createdAt, updatedAt }] }. Defaults to the calling agent's conversation.

channelId.description: Conversation whose subscriptions to list. Defaults to the calling agent's conversation.

tools.name: todo-list_share-io
tools.description: Create a public link to a task's output or input (or return the one you already created for it). Anyone with the link sees the task's CURRENT io without signing in: markdown as a web page titled with the task text, a file as the file itself. A form io or a task without that io fails with INVALID_STATE. Read members cannot share (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { shareId, publicUrl }.

io.description: Which io of the task: output or input.

tools.name: todo-list_get-io-share
tools.description: Get the public link you created for a task's output or input, if any. Read members cannot use it (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { shareId, publicUrl } or null.

io.description: Which io of the task: output or input.

tools.name: todo-list_unshare-io
tools.description: Revoke a public link to a task's output or input; the link answers 404 from then on. Only the user who created it can revoke it (FORBIDDEN). Returns: { ok: true }.

shareId.description: Share ID returned by share-io.

tools.name: todo-list_-subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe this conversation to one of this app's events (task_created, task_started, task_completed, task_blocked, task_state_changed, task_assigned, task_unassigned, task_planned, task_output_delivered, task_progress, task_updated, task_moved, task_deleted, agent_play_changed, agent_slots_changed, dependency_added, dependency_removed). Matching events are delivered here as they happen and wake the agent (self-wake guard: an agent is never woken by an event it caused itself). The subscription lives in the backend — it survives restarts of this app. Subscribing again to the same event REPLACES the previous filter. Returns: { subscription: { subscriptionId, topic, event, channelId, mode, filter, wakeUpOn, createdAt }, message }.

event.description: Local event name (the app namespace is implicit). Valid: task_created — A task (or group) was created in the to-do list.; task_started — A task entered the working state (autoplay start, start-node, or manual set-state).; task_completed — A task reached done or review (work finished). Carries the output reference when one was delivered.; task_blocked — A task was blocked, with its reason.; task_state_changed — A task moved between states (generic transition not covered by started/completed/blocked).; task_assigned — A task was assigned to an agent or workspace member.; task_unassigned — A task lost its assignee.; task_planned — A task was planned for a day (or taken off its day), optionally with a time.; task_output_delivered — A task delivered its output (markdown, form or file).; task_progress — A task reported progress (percentage) or a log note was added.; task_updated — A task's text, description, instructions or expected output changed.; task_moved — A task was moved to another parent or position in the tree.; task_deleted — A task (and its subtree) was deleted.; agent_play_changed — An autoplay runner's play was toggled.; agent_slots_changed — An autoplay runner's parallel slots changed.; dependency_added — A task now waits on another task (add-dependency) - the day/tree rows show the waiting semaforo until the blocker reaches done or cancelled.; dependency_removed — A task stopped waiting on another task (remove-dependency) - it becomes autoplay-eligible again at once.

filter.description: Optional filter. Fields AND-ed, values within a field OR-ed. Only the fields declared for the event are valid — see the event list.

wakeUpOn.description: Event names that wake the agent (response turn). Default: the subscribed event always wakes. Rarely needed with a single-event subscription.

channelId.description: Conversation that receives the events. Defaults to the calling conversation — omit it.

mode.description: notify = silent delivery, wake = trigger an agent response turn. Default: wake.

tools.name: todo-list_-unsubscribe
tools.description: Cancel this conversation's subscription(s) to this app's events. By subscriptionId, by event name, or — with neither — ALL of this conversation's subscriptions to this app. Idempotent. Returns: { unsubscribed, deleted?, channelId }.

event.description: Cancel the subscription to this event.

channelId.description: Defaults to the calling conversation.

tools.name: todo-list_-list-subscriptions
tools.description: List this conversation's subscriptions to this app's events, plus the app's event catalog (events, payload fields and valid filter fields) to subscribe to. Returns: { subscriptions: [...], events: [...] }.

channelId.description: Defaults to the calling conversation.
